answer: Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent forfeits only once. The identity then has to pass a marble challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next opal. Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. Registration requires a proof of work of 20 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the cipher. That is 20 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
